web_evidence.title: The House in the Pines — Penguin Random House
web_evidence.note: The publisher reproduces the complete prologue, which sustains experiential “you” narration through looking at, entering, sleeping in, and waking from the imagined house.

web_evidence.title: La casa entre los pinos — Fragmento
web_evidence.note: The publisher’s translated extract presents the complete second-person prologue followed immediately by sustained third-person narration of Maya in Chapters 1 and 2, directly demonstrating the person switch.

web_evidence.title: The House in the Pines Prologue-Chapter 8 Summary & Analysis
web_evidence.note: The structural analysis explicitly identifies the prologue as second-person narration and states that Chapter 1 switches to third-person limited narration, which is used for the rest of the novel.

person_note: The sustained novel from Chapter 1 onward uses third-person limited narration centered mainly on Maya. A complete second-person prologue addresses a reader-like narratee, but that single introductory exception does not override the person controlling the rest of the book. Numerous Goodreads passages support THIRD; confidence is medium because the strongest authorized material foregrounds the prologue/opening transition rather than providing whole-book coverage.
